questions.text: In an interest rate futures contract, the underlying is typically:
options: A government security or interest rate benchmark
questions.explanation: Interest rate futures are based on government securities or reference interest rate benchmarks.

questions.text: An investor invests ₹12,000 in a mutual fund at an NAV of ₹20. How many units will be allotted (ignoring loads and taxes)?
questions.explanation: Units allotted = Amount invested / NAV = 12,000 / 20 = 600 units. (But the question asks the correct option: 600 units.)

questions.text: If the compounding frequency increases from annual to quarterly, the effective annual rate (EAR):
questions.explanation: More frequent compounding increases the effective annual rate.

questions.text: Why should cash-flow statements be reviewed periodically?
options: Income and expenses remain constant always
To identify changes in income, expenses or new commitments early
questions.explanation: Regular review keeps the plan aligned with life changes and goals.

questions.text: National Pension System (NPS) is best described as:
options: A defined benefit scheme funded entirely by the government
A voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme regulated by PFRDA
A life insurance product regulated by IRDAI
questions.explanation: NPS is a voluntary defined contribution scheme regulated by PFRDA to help build a retirement corpus.

questions.text: Book building is a process used in:
options: Price discovery during IPOs and FPOs
questions.explanation: Book building is used to determine the issue price based on bids received from investors during public offers.

questions.text: Expected return of an individual security is calculated as:
options: Sum of potential returns divided by number of outcomes
Sum of possible returns weighted by their respective probabilities
Return on risk-free security plus risk premium
questions.explanation: Expected return is computed by summing potential returns multiplied by their probabilities.

questions.text: An increasing net worth over successive years indicates:
options: Financial progress and accumulation of assets
questions.explanation: Growing net worth shows positive wealth creation.

questions.text: If an investor’s KYC status shows 'On Hold', they must:
options: Submit required documents or updates to KRA
questions.explanation: ‘On Hold’ status indicates incomplete KYC; investor must update documents with the KRA to reactivate.

questions.text: An annuity is:
options: A series of equal payments made at regular intervals
questions.explanation: An annuity involves equal periodic payments or receipts.

questions.text: An Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) is best described as:
options: A retail mutual fund open to all investors
A privately pooled investment vehicle collecting funds from investors for defined investment policy
questions.explanation: AIFs are privately pooled investment vehicles that collect funds from investors to invest according to a defined policy for the benefit of investors.

questions.text: Systematic risk refers to:
options: Company-specific risk that can be diversified away
Market-wide risk that cannot be diversified
questions.explanation: Systematic risk arises from overall market factors and cannot be diversified.

questions.text: Stock brokers are required to be:
options: Registered with and regulated by SEBI and the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Brokers are SEBI-registered intermediaries and also members of stock exchanges.

questions.text: Ethics in investment advisory primarily relates to:
options: Moral principles that guide behaviour towards clients and markets
questions.explanation: Ethics refers to moral principles and standards that guide behaviour and decision-making, especially when dealing with client money and trust.

questions.text: PoA holders can redeem mutual fund units only if:
options: It is specifically authorized in the PoA document
AMC permits all PoA redemptions automatically
Units are held in physical form only
questions.explanation: Redemption authority must be explicitly stated in the Power of Attorney document.

questions.text: Commercial paper (CP) is best described as:
options: Short-term unsecured promissory note issued by corporates
questions.explanation: CP is an unsecured short-term instrument issued by corporates to meet working capital needs.

questions.text: The seller (writer) of a call option has:
options: The right to buy the asset
The obligation to sell the asset if the buyer exercises the option
The right to receive the asset for free
questions.explanation: The call writer must deliver the underlying (or cash equivalent) if the buyer exercises the option.

questions.text: Which of the following is consistent with fair dealing among clients?
options: Allocating investment opportunities equitably without unfair preference
Sharing one client’s strategy with another without consent
questions.explanation: Fair dealing means treating all clients fairly and equitably, without unfair preference or discrimination.

questions.text: An Investment Adviser must segregate advisory and distribution services to:
options: Comply with conflict of interest guidelines
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates segregation to avoid conflict between fee-based advice and commission-based product sales.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, an AMC can offer:
options: Both a value fund and a contra fund
Only a value fund but not a contra fund
Only a contra fund but not a value fund
Either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both
questions.explanation: A mutual fund house can have either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both, as per SEBI categorisation norms.

questions.text: A healthy DTI ratio for households is generally below:
questions.explanation: Debt payments above one-third of income can strain cash flows.

questions.text: Category I AIFs generally invest in:
questions.explanation: Category I AIFs include venture-capital, SME, social-venture and infrastructure funds that create positive economic impact.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: A client wanting to retire early at age 50 instead of 60 will generally need to:
options: Save more and invest more aggressively in earlier years
questions.explanation: Early retirement means fewer earning years and more retired years, requiring higher saving and often more growth-oriented investments.

questions.text: Preferred shareholders generally have:
options: Priority over equity shareholders in dividend and liquidation but limited voting rights
Higher returns than equity in all circumstances
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders get fixed dividends and priority in liquidation but limited or no voting rights.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common equity derivative traded on Indian exchanges?
options: Index futures and options on Nifty 50 and Sensex
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives such as Nifty 50 and Sensex futures/options are widely traded on NSE and BSE.

questions.text: For investments through stock exchange platforms, the transaction is settled through:
questions.explanation: Exchange-based mutual fund transactions are routed and settled through depositories and clearing corporations like NSDL/CDSL and ICCL/NCL.

questions.text: Ethical investing primarily involves:
options: Investing in sin industries for profit
Selecting investments based on personal moral principles
questions.explanation: Ethical investing filters out investments conflicting with an investor’s moral or ethical beliefs, such as gambling or tobacco.

questions.text: Which financial document summarises an individual’s assets, liabilities and net worth at a point in time?
options: Balance sheet or statement of net worth
questions.explanation: A personal balance sheet lists assets and liabilities and shows the person’s net worth.

questions.text: Dividend reinvestment option in mutual funds means:
options: Dividends are paid out to the investor’s bank account
Dividends are used to buy additional units in the same scheme
questions.explanation: Under the dividend reinvestment option, declared dividends are reinvested to purchase additional units in the same scheme.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of Modern Portfolio Theory?
options: Investors are rational and risk averse
Investors aim to maximize expected return for a given level of risk
Investors base decisions solely on expected return and risk
Investors prefer portfolios with the highest possible risk
questions.explanation: MPT assumes investors are rational and risk-averse, not risk-seeking; they prefer lower risk for the same level of return.

questions.text: Effective grievance redress mechanisms help in:
options: Improving investor trust and market integrity
questions.explanation: Robust grievance redress systems improve investor confidence, reduce disputes, and enhance market integrity.

questions.text: Bonus shares are issued:
options: For raising new capital from investors
Out of free reserves or retained earnings to existing shareholders
To employees as part of ESOPs
questions.explanation: Bonus shares are issued by capitalising reserves and giving additional shares to existing shareholders.

questions.text: Which of these is a good example of a SMART goal?
options: I want to be rich someday
I will save whatever is left at month end
I will invest ₹10,000 per month for 10 years to accumulate ₹20 lakh for my child’s education
I want to reduce my expenses
questions.explanation: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound; option C satisfies these criteria.

questions.text: Which of the following events is LEAST likely to trigger a review of a financial plan?
options: Minor fluctuation in one month’s expenses
questions.explanation: Small short-term expense fluctuations are normal; major life or financial changes warrant a plan review.

questions.text: Treynor Ratio differs from Sharpe Ratio because it uses:
options: Total risk instead of systematic risk
Systematic risk (beta) instead of total risk
questions.explanation: Treynor Ratio uses beta to measure systematic risk, while Sharpe Ratio uses standard deviation for total risk.

questions.text: Which of the following measures a stock’s sensitivity to market movements?
questions.explanation: Beta measures the stock’s volatility relative to the overall market.

questions.text: Net assets of a mutual fund scheme are defined as:
options: Face value of units multiplied by number of units
Total assets minus total liabilities and expenses of the scheme
Total market value of securities only
Total cash balance in bank accounts
questions.explanation: Net assets are arrived at by taking the current value of the portfolio plus current assets and subtracting expenses and liabilities of the scheme.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) is TRUE?
options: They require a minimum of ₹10,000 per month
They average out cost by regular periodic investing
They are available only to HNIs
questions.explanation: SIPs invest fixed amounts periodically, enabling rupee cost averaging and disciplined investing.

questions.text: Category III AIFs are characterised by:
options: Use of diverse or complex trading strategies including leverage
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs, such as hedge funds, employ complex or leverage-based trading strategies and invest in listed or unlisted securities.

questions.text: In a personal balance sheet, which of the following is a liability?
questions.explanation: Car loan is an obligation and hence liability.

questions.text: An investment of ₹10,000 grows to ₹14,641 in 4 years. The annual compound rate of return is approximately:
Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of a Portfolio Manager?
options: Maintaining client funds in a separate bank account
Investing unlimited amounts in associate companies
questions.explanation: A Portfolio Manager cannot invest more than 30% of client assets in associate or related entities, and must act in fiduciary capacity.

questions.text: The time value of money concept states that:
options: Money has constant value over time
Money available today is worth more than the same amount in future
Future money is always more valuable than money today
Time has no impact on money value
questions.explanation: A rupee today can be invested to earn returns, making it more valuable than a rupee received later.

questions.text: Which of these best describes holistic financial planning?
options: Coordinating investments, insurance, tax, retirement and estate aspects around the client’s life goals
Keeping all money in a savings account
questions.explanation: Holistic planning considers all aspects of the client’s financial life and integrates them around their goals.

questions.text: Transmission of mutual fund units occurs when:
options: Investor wants to transfer to a friend
Investor dies and legal heir claims ownership
questions.explanation: Transmission refers to the transfer of ownership of mutual fund units to legal heirs or nominees upon death of the holder.

questions.text: A puttable bond:
options: Allows the issuer to repay early at a lower price
Allows the investor to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-specified price on certain dates
questions.explanation: Puttable bonds give bondholders the right to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-set price, reducing interest rate risk for investors.

questions.text: Churning of client portfolios refers to:
options: Rebalancing as per agreed asset allocation
Excessive buying and selling primarily to earn higher fees or commissions
Investing in multiple funds for diversification
Switching from regular to direct plans
questions.explanation: Churning is unethical when trades are executed unnecessarily to generate more brokerage or fees, not to benefit clients.

questions.text: The cut-off price in a book-built issue means:
options: Lowest price bid by any investor
Highest price at which all shares can be allotted
questions.explanation: Cut-off price is the price at which the total demand matches the shares available for issue.

questions.text: Bid-ask spread is defined as:
options: Difference between current and previous day’s price
Difference between highest and lowest price of the day
Difference between bid price and ask price
Difference between issue price and face value
questions.explanation: Bid-ask spread = ask price − bid price.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a financial investment asset?
options: Gold jewellery used for personal wear
Equity shares of a listed company
questions.explanation: Equity shares are a financial investment asset. Gold jewellery and personal-use assets are primarily consumption assets, not pure financial investments.

questions.text: The main advantage of secured loans over unsecured loans is:
options: Lower interest rates due to collateral
questions.explanation: Collateral reduces lender’s risk, allowing lower interest rates.

questions.text: As the number of securities in a portfolio increases, the number of covariance terms:
questions.explanation: For n securities, the number of covariance terms is n(n–1)/2, which grows rapidly as portfolio size increases.

questions.text: Which is the MOST suitable investment for parking an emergency fund?
options: Liquid mutual fund or savings bank account
questions.explanation: Emergency funds must be readily accessible and low risk, so liquid funds or savings accounts are appropriate.

questions.text: The primary objective of SEBI is to:
options: Protect investor interests and regulate the securities market
questions.explanation: SEBI’s core objectives are investor protection, market regulation, and development of the securities market.

questions.text: Credit counselling agencies help borrowers by:
options: Advising on debt management and repayment plans
questions.explanation: They guide borrowers on budgeting, negotiations and repayment discipline.

questions.text: Household cash-flow deficit can be corrected by:
questions.explanation: Cash-flow balance improves by boosting inflows or cutting outflows.

questions.text: A high P/E ratio usually implies that:
options: Investors expect high growth or future earnings potential
questions.explanation: A high P/E often reflects investor optimism about future growth, though it can also indicate overvaluation.

questions.text: Under SCORES, complaints are first forwarded to:
questions.explanation: Complaints received on SCORES are first sent to the intermediary for response and resolution before SEBI’s further intervention.

questions.text: AIFs are primarily targeted at:
questions.explanation: Given the high minimum investment and risk profile, AIFs are intended for sophisticated and high-net-worth investors.

questions.text: A company’s dividend payout ratio is defined as:
options: Dividend per share ÷ earnings per share
Earnings per share ÷ dividend per share
questions.explanation: Dividend payout ratio = Dividend per share / EPS.

questions.text: If an individual saves ₹5,000 per month from ₹1,00,000 income, his annual savings ratio is:
The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.text: The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:
options: Prevent use of unpublished price-sensitive information for trading
questions.explanation: These regulations prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information to protect market integrity.

questions.text: Liquidity in the stock market means:
options: Ability to trade shares quickly without major price change
questions.explanation: Liquidity allows quick trade execution at stable prices.

questions.text: In the context of mutual fund transactions, RTA stands for:
questions.explanation: RTA stands for Registrar and Transfer Agent, entities that handle investor servicing and record maintenance for AMCs.

questions.text: The main advantage of maintaining a monthly budget is:
options: It ensures awareness of spending habits and helps achieve saving goals
questions.explanation: Monitoring cash flows leads to disciplined saving.

questions.text: Rematerialisation of mutual fund units refers to:
options: Converting demat units into physical statement form
questions.explanation: Rematerialisation means converting electronic demat holdings into physical statement form, usually to hold directly with AMC.

questions.text: Angel Funds are a sub-category of:
questions.explanation: Angel Funds are registered under Category I AIFs and invest in early-stage start-ups meeting specific criteria.

questions.text: For a conservative investor, equity allocation should generally be:
options: Aligned to risk profile, with lower equity and higher fixed income
questions.explanation: Conservative investors should have limited equity exposure, mainly using safer fixed-income assets.

questions.text: A closed-end mutual fund scheme:
options: Is generally listed on a stock exchange to provide liquidity
Always allows redemption directly with the AMC
questions.explanation: Closed-end schemes are for a fixed term and are mandatorily listed on a stock exchange so investors can exit by selling units there.

questions.text: Which of these is the PRIMARY role of commodities in a portfolio?
options: Act as an inflation hedge and diversifier
Offer voting rights in a company
questions.explanation: Commodities often act as an inflation hedge and help diversify a portfolio due to low correlation with traditional financial assets.

questions.text: Which of these is the least expensive form of credit?
questions.explanation: Gold loan is secured and typically has lower interest than unsecured credit.

questions.text: Over-leveraging occurs when:
options: Liabilities are disproportionately high compared to income or assets
questions.explanation: Excessive borrowing relative to capacity leads to financial strain.

questions.text: Portfolio optimization requires estimation of which parameters?
options: Expected returns, standard deviations, and correlation coefficients
questions.explanation: Portfolio optimization requires estimates of expected returns, risk (standard deviation), and correlation between securities.

questions.text: In the investor life cycle, the 'accumulation phase' is characterized by:
options: High net worth and focus on capital preservation
Building assets with higher risk tolerance and long horizon
questions.explanation: In the accumulation phase, investors are early in their careers, taking higher risk to build wealth over a long horizon.

questions.text: A key distinguishing feature of a mutual fund compared to PMS is that:
options: Mutual funds are unregulated, while PMS is regulated
Mutual funds pool money from many investors into a common portfolio, while PMS maintains segregated portfolios for each client
Mutual funds are only for HNIs, while PMS is for small investors
Mutual funds can invest only in equity
questions.explanation: Mutual funds operate a common pool of assets, whereas PMS typically runs segregated portfolios in each client’s name.

questions.text: Psychographic analysis of an investor helps in:
options: Understanding behavioural traits and risk personality
questions.explanation: Psychographic analysis identifies behavioural and personality characteristics affecting investment decisions and risk profile.

questions.text: The primary risk associated with investing in equities is:
options: Market volatility and loss of capital
questions.explanation: Equities are subject to market risk — price fluctuations due to company and economic factors.

questions.text: Which of the following is a liquidity constraint?
questions.explanation: Upcoming commitments like tuition or medical expenses create liquidity constraints requiring liquid assets.

questions.text: Which is an example of DIRECT investment by a retail investor?
options: Buying a diversified equity mutual fund
Investing through a PMS in multiple stocks
Buying listed shares of a company in her own demat account
Investing in a Category II AIF
questions.explanation: Buying shares directly in a demat account is a direct investment; mutual funds, PMS and AIFs are managed/pooled vehicles.

questions.text: Minimum net worth required for registration of a Portfolio Manager under SEBI (2020) Regulations is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: The minimum net worth requirement for an Investment Adviser (non-individual) is:
questions.explanation: Non-individual Investment Advisers must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹25 lakh as per SEBI (IA) Regulations.

questions.text: Which of the following intermediaries must maintain arm’s-length relationships between group entities?
questions.explanation: Both AMCs and Investment Advisers must maintain arm’s-length separation from distribution or related entities to avoid conflicts.

questions.text: If an investor receives ₹10,000 every year for 5 years, the present value at 8% p.a. is (approx.):
Under SEBI rules, portfolio managers cannot make investments in:
questions.explanation: SEBI prohibits PMS from investing in below-investment-grade securities to protect investors.

questions.text: An inverted yield curve, where short-term rates exceed long-term rates, often suggests:
options: Expectations of higher future growth and inflation
Market expectations of slowing growth or possible recession
That government debt is riskier than corporate debt
questions.explanation: Inverted yield curves are often interpreted as the market expecting future rate cuts, slowing growth or recession.

questions.text: A mutual fund is best described as:
options: A bank account where money is kept only in cash
An investment vehicle that pools money from investors to invest in a portfolio of securities
A company that gives fixed deposits with guaranteed returns
A government savings scheme with fixed interest
questions.explanation: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in a portfolio of securities such as equity, debt or gold, managed by an AMC.

questions.text: The process of valuing a mutual fund’s portfolio at current market prices on a regular basis is called:
questions.explanation: Mutual fund portfolios are marked to market so that NAV reflects current market prices of underlying securities.

questions.case_text: Arun invests ₹10,000 every year for 5 years in a recurring deposit earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Equal yearly deposits form an annuity.

questions.text: Future value after 5 years is approximately:
If deposits are made at beginning of each year, value will be:
questions.explanation: Annuity-due earns an extra period’s interest.

questions.text: If rate increases to 8%, corpus will:
questions.explanation: Higher rate ⇒ higher future value.

questions.text: If Arun skips one year’s deposit, final corpus will:
questions.explanation: Missing a payment reduces total contribution and compounding.

questions.case_text: Ravi, aged 36, works as a software engineer earning ₹1,40,000 per month. He had taken a 20-year home loan of ₹40 lakh five years ago at a fixed interest rate of 9.2% p.a. with an EMI of about ₹36,600. His outstanding principal today is ₹34 lakh. A bank is now offering him a floating-rate home loan at 8.1% p.a. for the remaining 15 years, with a one-time processing cost of ₹25,000.

questions.case_text: Manoj has a home loan of ₹40 lakh at 8.5% p.a. for 20 years. His EMI is ₹34,700. He also has a personal loan of ₹5 lakh at 12% for 3 years. Monthly income ₹1 lakh.

questions.text: If interest falls to 7.5% p.a., EMI reduces by about:
questions.explanation: Roughly ₹1 k drop per lakh interest cut on long-term loan.

questions.case_text: Arjun, aged 40, recently lost his job. He has ₹10 lakh in savings, monthly expenses of ₹60,000, and no outstanding loans. His priority is to sustain expenses while searching for new employment.

questions.case_text: Ritika plans to accumulate ₹10 lakh in 8 years for her MBA. She can invest in a debt fund giving 8% p.a. compounded annually.

If she invests ₹5 lakh today, how much will she have after 8 years?
If the fund compounds quarterly, the effective annual yield will:
